items.t: A leak from Russia’s federal statistics agency made it possible to estimate the country’s military death toll in the war against Ukraine. What else did it reveal?
items.m: At least 700,000 Russian service members have died in the war against Ukraine. Journalists from Meduza and Mediazona reached that figure using data that the hacker groups Belarusian Cyber Partisans and Silent Crow obtained when they broke into a database belonging to Rosstat, Russia’s federal statistics agency. It’s the first estimate to include service members listed as missing. Other researchers have also studied the hacked Rosstat data. Here’s what they found.

items.t: UK to invest £9.5m in Ukraine windfarm to bolster war-hit energy system
items.m: Project capable of powering 300,000 homes, with Britain having offered more than £770m to rebuild energy sector Britain will add to its multimillion pound investments in rebuilding Ukraine’s energy system by funding a windfarm project capable of powering 300,000 Ukrainian households. Ed Miliband, the UK foreign secretary, said Britain would invest £9.5m to build a 200 megawatt windfarm in an undisclosed location to bolster Ukraine’s energy reserves as its war with Russia approaches the five-year mark.
